question: Does confidence-based self-training with LightGBM, using unlabeled target-domain windows, beat a supervised MLP trained on the same few labels for HAR with 5 labels per activity?
method: Stratified 80/20 pool/test split (seed 42). 5 labeled rows per activity from the pool; remaining pool rows are unlabeled. Baseline: MLP on the shots. Improved: LightGBM self-trained with pseudo-labels (p>0.9, 3 rounds). Macro-F1 on the untouched test set, mean over seeds 42-44.
baseline: Supervised scikit-learn MLPClassifier (one hidden layer of 128, default Adam) trained only on the 5-shot labeled rows; stand-in for the paper's supervised deep HAR model.
improved: LightGBM classifier self-trained on the 5-shot labels plus confident pseudo-labels (max probability > 0.9) for unlabeled pool rows, iterated for 3 rounds.
notes: No hyper-parameter search was run: all settings are fixed a priori, so nothing was tuned on the test set (and no CV tuning was needed). Only 5 labels per class, so results vary with the shot sample; the std is over 3 seeds (population std). Scaler is fit on the pool, including unlabeled rows (no test leakage). The baseline is a stand-in, not the paper's NLP-label transfer method. Dataset is small (about 10k rows), so no subsampling was needed.
